result.topic_en: Draft on when a function can be represented by a trigonometric series whose coefficients eventually become infinitely small: a necessary condition via the twice-integrated function F, the converse, and a localisation statement using an auxiliary function ρ; the margins hold faint trigonometric side calculations.

methods.what: Second symmetric difference quotient of F, which must converge to f(x) as α, β → 0
Necessary condition: integral of cos μ(x-a) times an admissible function λ tends to zero as μ grows
Subtract linear and quadratic terms to make F periodic before expanding
Fourier coefficient formulas for the periodic part
Twice-integrated series expansion of the periodic part
Localisation: partial sums expressed via an integral over (b,c) involving the second derivative of the Dirichlet kernel and a cutoff function ρ

items.quote:
1) Zur Darstellbarkeit ist es nothwendig, dass es eine stetige
Function F(x) giebt
items.english: 1) For representability it is necessary that there exist a continuous function F(x) ...

items.quote:

so giebt es eine trigonometrische Reihe
items.english: 2) Conversely, if these two conditions are satisfied, there is a trigonometric series whose coefficients eventually become infinitely small and which represents the function wherever it converges.

items.quote: überall, wo sie convergirt, gegen fx convergirt.
items.english: The series A_0 + A_1 + A_2 ... converges to f(x) wherever it converges.
